gloss: wearing two hats; having two jobs or roles

definitions.gloss: wearing two hats; juggling two professions
definitions.explanation: Having two different occupations or roles simultaneously. Originally from the longer proverb {二足|にそく}のわらじを{履|は}く (to wear two pairs of straw sandals). Often used with the verb 履く.

examples.japanese: {二足|にそく}のわらじ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{履|は}いている→履く：00700_haku⟧。
⟦{医者|いしゃ}→医者：02847_isha⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{小説家|しょうせつか}→小説家：03070_shousetsuka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{二足|にそく}のわらじ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{履|は}く→履く：00700_haku⟧。
examples.english: To work as both a doctor and a novelist.

examples.japanese: ⟦{会社員|かいしゃいん}→会社員：03018_kaishain⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{農家|のうか}→農家：03539_nouka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{二足|にそく}のわらじ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{履|は}き→履く：00700_haku⟧⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧、⟦どちらも→どちらも：08721_dochiramo⟧⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{抜|ぬ}かない→抜く：02384_nuku⟧。
examples.english: While juggling the roles of office worker and farmer, she doesn't cut corners in either one.

notes:
Literally "two pairs of straw sandals." The full expression is {二足|にそく}のわらじ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{履|は}く→履く：00700_haku⟧ (to wear two pairs of sandals). Originates from the Edo period, when it was said that a person could not wear sandals for two different roles at the same time — specifically, a gambler could not also serve as a constable.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- A⟦と→と：00512_to⟧B⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{二足|にそく}のわらじ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{履|は}く→履く：00700_haku⟧: to hold the dual roles of A and B
- {二足|にそく}のわらじ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{活躍|かつやく}する→活躍する：25354_katsuyakusuru⟧: to be active in two roles

USAGE:
In modern usage, the expression has largely lost its negative connotation. It is now used admiringly to describe someone who successfully balances two demanding roles. The original proverb implied that trying to do two things at once meant neither would be done well.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{兼業|けんぎょう}→兼業：08562_kengyou⟧: side job, dual occupation — a more formal and neutral way to describe having two jobs
- ⟦{副業|ふくぎょう}→副業：08479_fukugyou⟧: side business — specifically a secondary job alongside a main job
- ⟦{二刀流|にとうりゅう}→二刀流：15543_nitouryuu⟧: two-sword style — used for someone excelling in two fields (popularized by baseball player Ohtani Shohei)
